name: Presa de Proserpina

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/509714147 (the point given for the guided tour, on the top of the dam's embankment 25 m behind the water face of the wall; heading = the water face, 90° from the line between the two ends of the OSM dam, 6.3°)

rights.note: Dam of the reservoir of Proserpina on the Arroyo de las Pardillas, Roman in origin (1st–2nd century AD) and raised and repaired in late-antique, medieval and 17th-century works; still in use. Builders unknown. Bien de Interés Cultural (1912) and part of the UNESCO World Heritage site «Archaeological Ensemble of Mérida» (1993).

sources.title: OpenStreetMap way 509714147 (waterway=dam: the water face of the wall, 417.5 m, its bends) (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL)

Embalse de Proserpina — Wikipedia (es): 427.8 m long, 21.6 m high, the screen wall of granite ashlar with a stepped batter on the water side and nine stepped buttresses against it, the earth embankment on the downstream side, the two intake towers on the downstream face

U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, «Proserpina Dam, plan and cross section» (Wikimedia Commons «Proserpina Dam.png»): 19 m high, 2.30 m at the top, about 5 m at the base, water face 1:10, buttresses with pinnacles, earthfill, the stretches of 227.9, 106.5 and 92.3 m, the two intake towers

Wikimedia Commons — «Embalse de Proserpina, Mérida (2015).JPG», «Proserpina dam - 1984.jpg», «Photo Prosperpina Dam Merida Spain 1955 - Touring Club Italiano 2 6269.jpg»: the stepped water face, the buttresses and their pinnacles
PNOA orthophoto, © Instituto Geográfico Nacional de España, CC BY 4.0 — the crest, the embankment behind it, the tops of the two towers and of the buttresses
Terrain: MDT05, © Instituto Geográfico Nacional de España, CC BY 4.0 (tools/terrain.py) — the reservoir at 244.0 m, the crest at 245.5 m, the surface of the embankment and the valley below it

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1818061_presa_de_proserpina.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The wall lofted along the OSM line (its water face): 2.3 m at the top, the water face stepped at 1:10, from the crest at 245.5 m (y = 1.5) down to its foundation (19 m at the deepest, following the valley towards the ends); nine stepped buttresses on the water face, evenly spaced (about 46 m), with small pinnacles above the crest (USBR section); the two intake towers on the downstream face of the wall, their tops just above the crest (x = −48 and +156, from the orthophoto); the earth embankment behind the wall, 45 m deep, its surface taken from the MDT05 (paths and trees left out). The origin is the point given for the guided tour (on the embankment), not on the wall itself: the water face is 25 m in front of it. Note: the buttresses stand on the water side and the towers on the dry side, as in Wikipedia, the USBR drawing and the orthophoto. With the reservoir at 244 m only the top 1.5 m of the water face shows; everything below is under water. Uncertain: the spacing of the buttresses and their size (±1 m), the positions and the shape of the towers' tops, the foundation. ground: keep with ground_fit false (a dam).
